orig_text:
DTLS Protocol Version 1.3.

              DTLS 1.3 ClientHello contains a
              supported_versions extension with 0x0304
              contained in its body and the ClientHello contains
              0xfefd in 'legacy_version'.
correct_text:
DTLS Protocol Version 1.3.

              DTLS 1.3 ClientHello contains a
              supported_versions extension with 0xfefc
              contained in its body and the ClientHello contains
              0xfefd in 'legacy_version'.
notes:
Per RFC 9147, Section 5.3 (ClientHello): "The supported_versions
entries for DTLS 1.0 and DTLS 1.2 are 0xfeff and 0xfefd (to match the
wire versions).  The value 0xfefc is used to indicate DTLS 1.3."

The value 0xfefc is therefore the DTLS 1.3 version value that a DTLS
1.3 ClientHello carries in its supported_versions extension; the value
0x0304 is the TLS 1.3 version value and only appears in the
supported_versions extension of TLS 1.3 ClientHellos (see Section 4.2.1
of RFC 8446).

The description in this enum incorrectly states that a DTLS 1.3
ClientHello "contains a supported_versions extension with 0x0304".
An implementation following this description would look for 0x0304 in
the supported_versions extension and would fail to identify any real
DTLS 1.3 ClientHello.

The same incorrect value appears in the corresponding prose paragraph of
this section: "DTLS 1.3 ClientHello messages are identified as having a
'legacy_version' of 0xfefd and a 'supported_versions' extension present
with 0x0304 as the highest version."  (The value 0xfefd in
'legacy_version' is correct.)
